newsitem.title: USA: Dinkins endorses ally for New York mayor.
newsitem.headline: Dinkins endorses ally for New York mayor.

text.p: Former Mayor David Dinkins, who recently considered a try at re-election, Thursday endorsed a Democratic ally in the party's quest to beat Republican incumbent Rudolph Giuliani.
Dinkins told reporters he would support Manhattan Borough President Ruth Messinger, a liberal who would be New York City's first woman mayor should she win November's election.
The former mayor said Wednesday he would not challenge the incumbent after indicating two weeks ago he might try to win back the job he lost to Giuliani in 1993.

"Pretty soon the incumbent will have to stop running from his own failed record because he has a formidable opponent in our candidate, one who doesn't keep harking back to the past but has a real vision for the future," Dinkins said.
Messinger, 56, Manhattan borough president since 1990, said she is running on a platform of improved education, public safety and economic development for New York City.

In accepting Dinkins' endorsement, she accused Giuliani of taking all the credit for the city's record crime drop, even though the crime rate was already declining during the previous Dinkins administration.
Her opponents in September's Democratic primary are Bronx Borough President Fernando Ferrer, black activist minister Al Sharpton and Brooklyn Councilman Sal Albanese.
Giuliani enjoys a comfortable lead in opinion polls over all four potential Democratic challengers.
